_comment: Defense Watch theater model: the Surge Simulator dataset. Built from the client's 2026-08-27 Theater Munitions-Expenditure and Advanced-Manufacturing Surge Uplift workbooks by data/scripts/build_theater_model.py. Do not hand-edit; fix the script or the archived source and rebuild. Production rates, surge multiples and expenditure are open-source estimates (CSIS, RAND, DoD budget documents, 2025-2026 press) and are cited per cell. Inventory figures are LOW to MEDIUM confidence open-source estimates used for relative readiness only; they are not, and must never be presented as, real stockpile counts. Every Epic Fury figure and any note tagged [IRAN-2026] is post-cutoff press reporting and NEEDS VERIFICATION before publication.
_revision: 2026-09-14: first build. Replaces scenarios_new.json as the simulator input once the engine is switched over. Site munition ids kept where a line already existed (tlam, jav, sting); client_key carries the workbook key.

_schema.weapons[].surge_production_per_year: round(current x surge_multiple); optimistic-but-real announced target plus new-entrant capacity
_schema.weapons[].available_inventory_units: open-source estimate, see inventory_confidence; relative readiness only
_schema.weapons[].industrial_base: names in rankings_new.json to link the line to company pages
_schema.theaters[].expenditure[id].units_90d: US rounds expended over a ~90-day full campaign
_schema.theaters[].expenditure[id].tag: ANCHOR = pinned to a published figure; ANCHOR* = published opening-phase figure extended to 90 days; MODEL = modelled from rates or analogy
_schema.theaters[].type: shock = short ferocious fight; grind = protracted attrition. Display label, drives nothing

model.horizon_formula: available_inventory_units / (burn_per_day - production_per_day); SUSTAIN when production_per_day >= burn_per_day; null when units_90d is 0
model.lead_time_policy: base_lead_months and advanced_lead_months are recorded per weapon but NOT applied. This matches the client workbook, whose Sustainment Horizon sheet applies the surge rate from day 1 and does not reference its lead-time columns. Pending client confirmation (raised 2026-09-14).
model.multi_theater: expenditure is the arithmetic sum of taiwan + korea + baltic (client rule)
model.expected_horizons: data/theater_model.expected.json holds every cell computed with horizon_formula; the engine acceptance test must reproduce it

theaters.label: Taiwan Strait
theaters.description: All-out invasion of a fortified island by the world's 2nd-largest military. A naval, air and long-range-strike fight: anti-ship missiles, standoff strike and fleet air defense dominate, with only a marginal artillery role. Per CSIS wargaming, the available anti-ship inventory is expended within the first week.

tlam.note: Land-attack + Maritime-Strike anti-ship; subset of the ~5,000 LR-PGM bucket.

pac3.note: Guam/Japan/Okinawa base defense vs DF-21/DF-26 salvos.

sm3.note: Limited: few PRC MRBMs range US ships; some Guam/Aegis BMD.

sm6.note: Fleet air/missile defense + anti-surface; DMO surface engagements.

amraam.note: Intense air-to-air: wargame loses hundreds of aircraft; heavy AAM expenditure.

jassm.note: Standoff strike on invasion fleet+airfields; part of the ~5,000 long-range PGMs CSIS wargame expends in 3 wks.

thaad.note: Guam terminal defense vs PRC MRBM.

lrasm.note: Entire available anti-ship inventory expended in ~week 1 (CSIS First Battle wargame; LRASM the pacing shortage).

m155.note: US artillery role modest; Taiwan+USMC littoral fires.

theaters.label: Korean Peninsula
theaters.description: A massive artillery duel against thousands of dug-in tubes ranged on Seoul, plus dense ballistic-missile defense against DPRK SRBM and MRBM salvos. Sustained for months: artillery and interceptors are the long poles.

pac3.note: Dense DPRK SRBM threat (KN-23/24/25); exceeds US-available annual allocation.

amraam.note: Air superiority vs numerous but low-quality DPRK air force.

thaad.note: DPRK MRBM (Nodong); exceeds a full year of production.

lrasm.note: Small DPRK navy; limited anti-ship demand.

m155.note: US share of counter-battery vs ~14,000 DPRK tubes; Ukraine analog ~6-10k/day combined, US ~1,700/day x 90.

theaters.label: NATO Baltic (Art. 5)
theaters.description: Russia invades a NATO member (Poland, Finland or the Baltics). A ground-and-air war of attrition modelled on Ukraine consumption: 155mm dominates, with anti-tank, short-range air defense, SEAD and missile defense. Demand only intensifies.

m155.note: Ukraine analog: 6,000-10,000 rounds/day; US/NATO share ~2,800/day x 90 (RAND: 14-21 brigades to expel).

jav.note: Anti-armor vs Russian mechanized; Ukraine consumed thousands.

theaters.label: INDOPACOM Maritime
theaters.description: A sustained sea-control campaign across the Western Pacific. Anti-ship, standoff strike and fleet air and missile defense weapons, fired in pulses as engagements flare. Long enough for production ramps to matter.

tlam.note: Maritime-Strike + land attack across the theater.

sm3.note: BMD vs PRC anti-ship ballistic missiles (DF-21D/DF-26).

sm6.note: Anti-ship + fleet air defense (primary DMO magazine).

lrasm.note: Entire available inventory (competes with Taiwan for same magazines).

theaters.label: Multi-Theater
theaters.description: Taiwan, Korea and a Baltic Article 5 trigger at once. Every category is drawn down simultaneously from one industrial base and demand never relents: the defining worst case. Demand is the arithmetic sum of the three concurrent theaters.

tlam.note: Superposition of concurrent Taiwan + Korea + Baltic demand (Iran/Maritime would add more).

theaters.label: Epic Fury
theaters.description: The 2026 Iran campaign continued for another 90 days at its February to April intensity. Interceptors and standoff strike weapons that were already depleted in the 39-day campaign keep burning, several beyond their remaining inventory.

tlam.note: 39-day campaign fired >1,000 (mostly opening salvos); +~400 sustained over the +51d continuation. [IRAN-2026: needs verification]

pac3.note: >=45% of US Patriot inventory in 39 days; continuation draws down remaining stock + new production. [IRAN-2026]

sm6.note: Part of the >100 combined SM-3/SM-6 reported; sustained naval BMD. [IRAN-2026]

jassm.note: 39-day ~1,100 JASSM-ER (largest ever); +~500 continuation. EXCEEDS ~1,500 remaining inventory. [IRAN-2026]

thaad.note: 39-day >150 (incl 2025 Twelve-Day War); Iran keeps firing ballistic missiles -> +~150. EXCEEDS ~250 inventory. [IRAN-2026]

lrasm.note: Not used vs Iran; CSIS: LRASM inventory 'largely unaffected'. [IRAN-2026]

harm.note: Heavy SEAD vs Iranian IADS early, sustained through continuation.
